deep.reconstruction:
Context: E477 is the founding paper on double zeta values. Euler works with sums of the form Σ_{x≥y≥1} 1/(x^a y^b), which include the diagonal terms x=y; in modern notation these are ζ*(a,b). On this page, for a fixed weight ('ordinis exponens') N, q^μ denotes ζ*(μ, N−μ) and p^N denotes ζ(N). The stated side condition q^μ + q^{N−μ} = p^μ·p^{N−μ} + p^N is the harmonic-product (stuffle) relation in its starred form, ζ*(a,b) + ζ*(b,a) = ζ(a)ζ(b) + ζ(a+b). Euler has a general linear relation, obtained earlier from a partial-fraction expansion, depending on two parameters m and n with N = m+n. Section 28 specialises m; section 29 specialises n.

Case m=4 (weight n+4). The relation is 0 = q^4 − n(q^3+q^{n+1}) + C(n+1,2)(q^2+q^{n+2}) − C(n+2,3)(q+q^{n+3}) + n(n²+5)/6·p^{n+4} + Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} C(k+3,3) q^{n−k} − C(n+3,4) p^{n+4}. Two things happen in the rearrangement:
- The q^1 terms cancel.
- The p-coefficient becomes C(n+3,4) − n(n²+5)/6 = n(n−1)(n²+3n+14)/24.
The result is q^n + 4q^{n−1} + … + C(n+1,3) q² + q^4 − n(q^3+q^{n+1}) + C(n+1,2)(q^2+q^{n+2}) − C(n+2,3) q^{n+3} = n(n−1)(n²+3n+14)/24 · p^{n+4}. The second printed line belongs to the left-hand side, continuing it, exactly as in the m=3 layout on the previous page.

Section 29, case n=1 (weight m+1).
- For even m all terms cancel, so the relation is an identity.
- For odd m, i.e. even weight N, it gives Σ_{k=2}^{m} (−1)^k ζ*(k, N−k) = ½ ζ(N).
- Check at N=4: ζ*(2,2) − ζ*(3,1) = 7/4 ζ(4) − 5/4 ζ(4) = ½ ζ(4).

Section 29, case n=2 (weight m+2). Euler writes the general relation with ± signs according to the parity of m; the next page lists the specialisations.
- At m=2 it reduces to q² − q³ = ½ p⁴.
- At m=3 the next page gives 3q² + q³ − 3q⁴ = 3p⁵. I checked this with the known weight-5 values: 3(11/2 ζ5 − 2ζ2ζ3) + (3ζ2ζ3 − 9/2 ζ5) − 3(3ζ5 − ζ2ζ3) = 3ζ5. Correct.

Purpose: to produce linear relations among double zeta values of a fixed weight, in modern terms consequences of the double shuffle. These are used to evaluate the sums in terms of products of zeta values, especially when the weight is odd.
errors: No mathematical errors found on this page. The m=4 coefficient n(n−1)(n²+3n+14)/24 checks out, and the n=1 and n=2 specialisations are consistent with each other (both give q²−q³=½p⁴ at weight 4).
The printed side condition reads 'q^μ + q^{n+4−μ} = p^μ + p^{n+4}'. Mathematically this must mean ζ(μ)ζ(N−μ) + ζ(N), i.e. a product (or Euler's own abbreviation for one), not p^μ + p^N.

ideas.what: Starred stuffle relation q^μ + q^{N−μ} = ζ(μ)ζ(N−μ) + ζ(N)
ideas.modern_name: Harmonic (stuffle) product for double zeta values
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477); systematised by Hoffman, Zagier and others in the 1990s

ideas.what: Linear relations among ζ*(μ, N−μ) at fixed weight, from partial fractions, specialised to m=4 with closed-form binomial coefficients
ideas.modern_name: Double shuffle relations / Euler's decomposition formula

ideas.what: For even weight N: Σ_{k=2}^{N−1} (−1)^k ζ*(k, N−k) = ½ ζ(N)
ideas.modern_name: Alternating (parity) sum relation for double zeta values
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler; reappears in modern double-zeta literature

deep.surprise_reason: Routine specialisations of Euler's well-studied double-zeta relations in E477, a paper heavily analysed in the modern multiple-zeta literature. Nothing here appears new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: 29.I: the bracketed p^{m+1} coefficient is a stacked expression meaning (½ ± ½), i.e. 1 for even m and 0 for odd m. It is not '±½]'. Only with this reading do the stated conclusions (identity for even m, ½p^{m+1} for odd m) follow.
m=4 'siue' formula: the line '+q^4 − n(q^3+q^{n+1}) + …' is a continuation of the left-hand side, not part of the right-hand side.
The side condition 'p^μ + p^{n+4}' should be read as product ζ(μ)ζ(n+4−μ) plus ζ(n+4) (possibly Euler's own shorthand).
